offline_preparation.scope: Closed source-graph inventory, representative conversion plus zero-reject full 204-root recursive intake with unresolved rice terrain edits preserved but disabled, and checked era/topology/terrain/crop strategy only. L19 contains two independent tracks bundled only for convenience: farms/irrigation must prove all 16 adjacency masks across every irrigable terrain family, while the base-terrain track must replace the Terrain Lab's grassland fallback for Civ III tundra (base 3) with normalized tundra base-color, height, and specular channels regardless of irrigation state. Irrigated and unirrigated tundra plus mixed tundra/non-tundra material boundaries must appear at both zooms. Neither track may depend on the other; no L19 rendering, final adjacency mapping, or ownership has been performed by offline preparation.

steps.title: Goody huts and colony outposts with 192-tile promotion approval

offline_preparation.scope: Exact three-root goody-hut conversion, strict recursive three-root preindustrial plus three-root industrial colony-outpost conversion, 8-bucket hut selection, viewer visibility, owner/era/extraterritorial colony semantics, restrained owner-color marker, resource coexistence, rotation, and night attachments. Corrected matrix-order evidence closes the stale industrial rejection below 8e-7 without a static bake; no L19A rendering or ownership.

steps.title: Remaining tile infrastructure and 192-tile promotion approval

offline_preparation.scope: Approved source-backed Fort/Barricade, exact Airstrip, era-aware Outpost, watchtower-derived Radar Tower, restrained source fort pole/bunting Victory Location, and feathered static Pollution/Crater ground-state presentation across all four eras/owners, routes, relief, day/night, isolation, and both zooms. Flat observatory plaza, Modern Fort, missile silo, opaque pollution tile replacement, and all transient effects remain rejected. Runtime ownership is inactive until I19B.

steps.title: Units and animation and 192-tile promotion approval

offline_preparation.scope: Five-family non-Warrior static conversion including a multi-mesh naval body, eight-action basic semantic contract, 37 unique raw clips/44 logical bindings, 93 deduplicated model-aware component pose caches serving 100 logical component/action bindings, pose-versus-motion policy, native timing and attack-slot alias policy, quantized skin-weight evidence, facing strategy, runtime-selected Civ III owner-color contract, an authoritative two-child Army contract using dedicated Great General art, and a generic arbitrary-tree compiler for Horseman, Classical Great General, Catapult, and Tank producing eight independently animated nodes, four resolved sockets, 30 components, 50 textures, 52 unique converted node/action clips, 62 logical bindings across 31 actions, 52 deterministic model-aware pose caches, and four-phase zero-separation proof. Worker specialty preparation covers all 13 authoritative Job_ID values, state fallbacks, CAPTURE and generic BUILD, an exclusive action-selected tool group, and 11 structurally validated normalized Builder work/repair/capture clips. Horseman, Tank, and Classical General cover all eight basic actions; Catapult death remains an explicit truthful-art gap. The executable calibration contract covers eight Civ III facings and both 128x64/64x32 zoom bases, freezes single-body default/optional humanoid triad/Army two-body formation policy, and records an exact installed-GOG body-only replacement boundary without enabling it; no L20 rendering gate, actual all-facing/both-zoom visual measurements, final scale/facing-offset approval, Catapult death selection, Builder body/tool binding, worker VFX calibration, or runtime unit ownership transfer.

steps.title: Complete 192-tile beauty scene and final user visual approval

milestones.title: Paired Game Integration gates
milestones.pairing_rule: Each I# consumes only the frozen, approved L# handoff with the same suffix. Lab owns appearance; Integration owns authoritative game state, placement, caching, compositing, exclusive suppression, telemetry, reset behavior, and hard failure without native replay.

promotion_prerequisites.rule: Each system waits only for its matching Renderer Lab technical gate and required visual approval, then passes an independent game-integration gate. L21 is a final combined release gate, not a global integration prerequisite.

steps.title: Render infrastructure and tile-bound overlays
scope: As each matching lab gate is approved, consume its frozen pack, definition, scene, reference, ownership, cache-input, and custom-coverage handoff without waiting for unrelated lab systems.

Game-integrate rivers, roads, railroads, farms/irrigation, mines, goody huts, colonies, fortresses, barricades, airfields, outposts, radar towers, pollution, craters, and victory locations as independently gated families.
Resolve authoritative Civ III topology, terrain, era, owner/civilization or culture selectors where applicable without transferring gameplay ownership to the renderer.
Give every family independent definition resolution, exclusive custom-on ownership, retained-layer ordering, and visible hard failure without native replay.
acceptance: Road and railroad fixtures cover every reachable connection mask, slopes, junctions, crossings, wrapping, both zooms, and coexistence without cracks, doubled segments, or unstable selection.

Farm/irrigation and mine fixtures cover every reachable terrain and state family, deterministic variants, season/environment response, grounding, occlusion, and both zooms without changing gameplay state.

Goody-hut fixtures cover all eight deterministic reference buckets, visible/hidden viewer states, wrap duplication, grounding, diagonal facing, and day/night attachments; colony fixtures cover all four owner eras, owner/territory mismatch, restrained owner color, stable resource-clear placement, and same-tile resource readability.

Remaining-infrastructure fixtures cover Fortress/Barricade distinction, all four Airfield/Outpost era profiles, owner color, both zooms, rotation, relief, clipping/wrap, day/night runway lights, persistent Pollution/Crater state, Radar Tower, and Victory Location readability.
Configuration off restores the complete native draw; configuration on makes a missing or failed integrated family fail the custom frame without native substitution.

The production infrastructure fixture composes roads, rails, farms, mines, goody huts, colonies, remaining tile infrastructure, resources, terrain, and retained Civ III overlays with stable depth and zero native fallback.
must_not: Do not start a family's production ownership before that family's own lab gate and visual approval pass.
Do not infer connectivity, yields, resource presence, production, depletion, worker activity, or other gameplay facts from rendered geometry.
Do not transfer a family to its I# gate until the complete replacement instance or network segment set is ready.

steps.title: Render resources with visibility and animation
scope: Use the validated 26-resource BIQ mapping seed to compile normalized Civ VI/source candidates while allowing scenario and user definitions to replace every target.
Capture authoritative resource ID/name/class, selected map PCX index, tile/pixel anchor, terrain context, and player-specific visibility/fog state.
Render only map resource bodies, shadows, and explicitly mapped ambient animation; retain all native non-map resource icons.
Support terrain-specific visual variants and stable absolute-time animation with exclusive custom-on resource-body ownership.
acceptance: Every loaded BIQ map resource has complete custom coverage, including scenario-defined resources absent from the 26-entry vanilla seed.
Fixtures prove hidden strategic resources are never revealed and visible resources preserve anchors, terrain variants, depth, fog, hour/season, and deterministic animation.
Missing or failed custom-on replacements fail visibly without restoring a native map body or affecting retained non-map icons.
Civilopedia, city-screen, trade-network, advisor, diplomacy, notification, and every other non-map resource icon remain native and unchanged.
must_not: Do not replace or mutate resources.pcx globally merely to suppress a map resource draw.
Do not derive discovery, visibility, yields, trade, prerequisites, depletion, placement, or AI behavior from source art.
Do not treat a low-confidence stand-in such as Rubber to Cocoa as an immutable runtime mapping or completed asset conversion.
Do not transfer map-resource ownership until the complete replacement set is ready.

steps.title: Render culture, era, and size-specific cities
scope: After L17 and its visual approval, consume the accepted city matrix across owner/civilization identity, culture group, all reachable eras, and Civ III city sizes without waiting for unrelated lab gates.
Port the accepted city footprint, terrain grounding, depth/occlusion envelope, both-zoom calibration, and retained native label/population/UI envelope into production contracts.
Production-integrate walls, capital status, city style, and visible building/wonder composition from the accepted lab result.
Bind city-model emissive groups, windows, lamps, and static analytic lights to the shared M6.4 environment.
Describe city-owned flame, smoke, steam, or beacon attachments for M7.5 execution without duplicating their scheduler.
acceptance: Fixtures cover every reachable size and era with representative civilizations/culture groups, owner color, walls/capital/style states, both zooms, terrain grounding, scrolling/wrapping, depth, and retained-label envelopes.
Representative culture, era, and size fixtures activate the correct windows and lamps across day/night without swapping geometry or relighting retained labels/UI.
Custom-on failure removes every renderer-owned city light/effect together with the replacement body, reports a hard failure, and never restores the native city body.
must_not: Do not bake all night behavior into duplicate city models or let a city-owned effect survive custom-frame failure.
Do not take ownership of Civ III city labels, population displays, or HUD.

steps.title: Render animated units and movement/combat states
scope: After L20 and its visual approval, consume the accepted static, directional, skeleton, clip, movement, combat, stacking, and interruption results without waiting for unrelated lab gates or redesigning their art direction during production integration.
Capture stable unit and action/event IDs, eight-direction facing, action/clip state, timing, loop/completion policy, hit points, visibility, stack order, and current/active/selected flags.

Capture the native viewer-conditioned display civilization and its Leader.Color_Table_ID, and populate one palette LUT from Civ III's effective loaded Units_Image_Data color tables so scenarios and hidden-nationality presentation remain authoritative.

Capture and composite unit bodies in Civ III's Animator-owned Units_Control dynamic plane using its visible-unit order, wrap-aware interpolated pixel origins, clipping, and unioned dirty rectangles; terrain m19 unit fields remain descriptive only.
Interpolate movement between authoritative Civ III tile and pixel anchors using captured segment progress, including scrolling and map-wrap representations.
Synchronize idle, fidget, run, fortify, attack, bombard, victory, death, capture, worker, and scenario-defined clips without deriving gameplay timing from rendered frames.

Compose mounted and crewed units through one pack-defined parent/child/socket schema, using the resolved Rider, Operator, defender, and TankGunner recipes without unit-name branches or duplicate HUD instances.
Replace only the vanilla unit body sprite while retaining Civ III ownership of the selection cursor/ring, green health bar, left-side activity/status marks, stack indicators, and related unit HUD.

Before implementing replacement, prove the smallest supported-build boundary around Unit.tick_anim's direct FLC body blit; record any concretely required patch symbol and addresses through the dependency ledger.
Capture the anchors and selected/current state needed to keep all retained native unit overlays aligned above and around the moving 3D body.
acceptance: Timestamped fixtures cover all eight directions, movement endpoints, attack/target state, fortify transitions, victory/death lifecycle, and skipped-frame determinism.
Stable event IDs prevent clips from restarting on redraw, while interruption tests cover combat, death, selection/stack changes, visibility, loading, and renderer reset.

Owner-color fixtures cover multiple leaders sharing one converted unit, captures and alternate color assignments, partial scenario ntp overrides, barbarians, and hidden-nationality views without rebuilding meshes, materials, or clips or exposing the actual owner.

The native selected-unit underlay, health bar, activity/status marks, stack indicators, and related unit HUD follow the correct stacked unit through movement, scrolling, clipping, combat, and selection changes and preserve the required z-order.
Body suppression leaves every retained native overlay visible exactly once and does not apply renderer lighting, color grading, or replacement ownership to it.
Missing models or clips fail the custom unit pass visibly without restoring the vanilla unit body; retained native overlays remain outside body ownership and gameplay continues.
must_not: Do not move, remove, damage, select, target, or complete an action independently of Civ III.
Do not shorten or extend Civ III gameplay waits until an audited synchronization hook can signal equivalent completion.
Do not accumulate animation progress by rendered-frame count or draw the selection underlay beneath the wrong stacked unit.
Do not bake moving units into the retained terrain bitmap or drive unit placement from the first unit found in a terrain-tile iterator.
Do not suppress, duplicate, replace, relight, recolor, or occlude Civ III's native selection, health, activity/status, stack, or related unit HUD during M7.4.

steps.title: Render transient effects and synchronized projectiles

boundary_audit.pixel_suppression: Tick and native sound run before FLC byte 0x184 gates the direct blit; ordinary effects reuse the existing animated-effect loader, while standalone SDI needs the animation loader upgraded to inlead.
boundary_audit.nuclear_outcomes: Unit_do_nuke_tile is detonation and Unit_get_intercepted_as_nuke is interception in offline play and multiplayer replay; delivery animation is not an outcome.

scope: Capture stable effect event IDs, source/target anchors, spawn timestamp, duration, normalized progress, outcome, interruption, and cleanup policy.
Synchronize projectiles, impacts, combat particles, explosions, nuclear effects, worker effects, and ambient map effects to Civ III events while audio remains Civ III-owned initially.

For bombard and bombing, derive release children from authored unit-action markers and impact children from Civ III's exact AE_Hit/AE_Miss/AE_WaterMiss creation calls; keep Fire Rate impact count distinct from decorative release count.
Treat nuclear delivery, interception, detonation, fallout/scorch presentation, and victim removal as an explicit separate event family rather than a scaled ordinary explosion.
Execute visible model attachments such as flames, smoke, sparks, steam, flickering lights, and beacons using M6.4 assets and M5.3 absolute-time scheduling.
acceptance: Deterministic event traces prove spawn, flight, impact, interruption, cleanup, and skipped-frame behavior without duplicate or orphaned effects.
Effect ownership and hard-failure behavior prevent duplicate vanilla/replacement visuals and preserve Civ III gameplay timing.

Fixtures cover ballistic land hit, land miss, water miss, air bomb, guided missile, multiple Fire Rate impacts, both nuclear outcome branches, and preservation of Civ III-owned effect audio while only native pixels are suppressed.
Hidden, off-screen, daylight-disabled, paused, failed, and completed ambient attachments request no frames; visible active attachments remain bounded and deterministic.
must_not: Do not infer combat outcomes, targets, or cleanup from renderer frame count.
Do not play duplicate replacement audio or keep the redraw loop active for invisible completed effects.

steps.title: Automate seasonal asset authoring and validation
Add production human and AI-assisted visual review workflow
Inventory and map effective C3X natural wonders
scope: Parse the effective scenario, user, or default natural-wonder replacement set and enumerate every dynamic definition and placed NATURAL_WONDER_DISTRICT_ID instance from authoritative C3X state.

Capture stable natural-wonder ID/name, tile/pixel anchor, terrain and adjacency requirements/direction, native PCX row/column, configured hour/season/direction animations, visibility/fog, label eligibility, and custom-coverage metadata.

Inventory Civ VI Base/DLC Features, TerrainStyle NaturalWonders, Clutter, VFX, water, Landmarks, and cooked package references and seed exact, approximate, unavailable, or authored mappings with source-part and footprint evidence.
acceptance: Every effective definition and placed instance is classified; the checked-in 18 definitions are treated only as a seed rather than a fixed completeness claim.
Every native sprite cell, configured animation alternative, terrain/adjacency/direction condition, and retained label/fog responsibility has explicit mapping and complete-coverage evidence.
Ordinary BIQ landmark terrain, mountains, and volcanoes are not classified as natural wonders without an authoritative C3X natural-wonder instance.
must_not: Do not infer natural-wonder identity from terrain appearance, landmark state, filename similarity, or Civ VI source footprint.
Do not modify placement, generation, yields, passability, worker restrictions, visibility, or other natural-wonder gameplay.

steps.title: Render terrain-integrated natural-wonder kits
scope: Render source-agnostic kits containing main geometry, terrain blend, directional pieces, clutter, water, emissives/lights, and ambient effects from one authoritative C3X anchor.
Normalize useful multi-part or multi-tile source art as visual overhang without creating gameplay tiles or suppressing independently owned neighboring content.
Use shared environment and absolute-time scheduling for waterfalls, geysers, steam, volcanic effects, waves, mist, and similar visible animation, with exclusive per-instance custom ownership.
Retain the native natural-wonder name label plus Civ III fog/shroud, borders, grid, cursor, minimap, HUD, and UI above the replacement.
acceptance: Deterministic two-size fixtures cover land, mountain, geothermal/volcanic, coastal, and water examples across direction, adjacency, noon/night, seasons, animation, scrolling/wrapping, clipping/depth, and source-multipart cases.
Static instances request no continuous redraw and animated effects retain deterministic phase across skipped frames, pause, reset, visibility, and failure.

Every effective custom-on instance draws one complete 3D kit or fails visibly without native body/legacy-animation replay, while the retained native name label and other retained layers remain visible exactly once.
must_not: Do not transfer a natural wonder to custom ownership before all required replacement pieces are ready.
Do not relight, bloom, duplicate, suppress, or replace the native natural-wonder label or other retained Civ III layers.
Do not let visual footprint, VFX, or animation alter C3X game state or timing.

steps.title: Inventory and map constructed wonders
scope: Enumerate every loaded BIQ Great and Small Wonder and every effective default, user, and scenario C3X wonder-district definition.
Classify mapless, planned, constructing, completed, destroyed, abandoned, obsolete, orientation, and visibility states with stable BIQ and tile identities.
Seed swappable Civ III-to-Civ VI/source mappings without placing source-specific formats in runtime packs.
acceptance: Every BIQ wonder and effective C3X wonder config entry is classified with mapping confidence and map-visibility evidence.
The inventory distinguishes BIQ identity, source sprite cells, construction/completion art, alternate direction, calibration, and custom-ownership readiness.
must_not: Do not invent map placement for a wonder without an authoritative C3X Wonder District tile.
Do not treat a checked-in config block count as complete effective scenario coverage.

steps.title: Render constructed wonders
scope: Render source-agnostic construction and completed wonder models at authoritative C3X Wonder District anchors.

Support alternate orientation, terrain/river/city placement, environment, emissive groups, analytic lights, ambient-effect attachments, destruction/abandonment, layering, and exclusive custom-on ownership.
acceptance: Deterministic fixtures cover construction, completion, orientation, destruction/abandonment, day/night emissives/effects, seasons, and missing assets.
Configuration off preserves the existing C3X wonder draw; custom-on failed replacement reports a hard failure without restoring it.
must_not: Do not complete, destroy, relocate, obsolete, or otherwise mutate a wonder from renderer state.
Do not transfer native C3X wonder art to custom ownership until the complete replacement instance is ready.

steps.title: Inventory effective C3X districts and render states
scope: Enumerate every built-in, dynamic, user, and scenario district definition after C3X config precedence is applied.

Capture stable instance/type identity, owner, culture, era, render strategy, effective dependent-building set/count, construction, damage, abandonment, visibility, terrain, coast orientation, and topology state.
Seed district-base, building-attachment, count-preset, and topology mappings from useful Civ VI/source ArtDefs.
acceptance: All effective district definitions and every renderer-relevant state family are classified with scenario precedence and source evidence.

The inventory represents shared-district building additions as the effective C3X visual set and distinguishes ordinary, Wonder, Natural Wonder delegation, Bridge, Canal, Great Wall, Port, and other special families.
must_not: Do not duplicate C3X district gameplay, city-sharing, yield, passability, construction, or building ownership logic in the renderer.
Do not infer complete district coverage from the checked-in 21 default definitions.

steps.title: Render composite district kits
scope: Render a source-agnostic district base plus independently mapped building attachments for by-building strategies.
Resolve by-count strategies to deterministic monolithic or attachment-set stage presets.
Use authored sockets where available and deterministic collision-aware placement otherwise, with exclusive per-instance custom ownership.
Let each base, building attachment, or count preset own the emissive groups, analytic lights, and ambient effects that it visually introduces.
acceptance: Fixtures prove individual building additions appear without replacing unrelated components and remain stable across redraw, save/load, season, and machine.
A missing required base, attachment, or preset fails the custom district pass visibly without restoring the native C3X district draw.
Adding or removing a represented building activates or removes only its owned windows, lamps, flames, smoke, or steam across day/night.
must_not: Do not require Civ VI district file organization to mirror C3X PCX columns or expose Civ VI formats at runtime.
Do not accidentally mix partial 3D and native district layers under replace ownership.

steps.title: Complete special district and final integration gates
scope: Implement Bridge, Canal, and Great Wall connection pieces, Port coastline alignment, Wonder District relationships, and construction/damage/abandonment variants.
Complete scenario override, environment, layering, performance, custom-on hard-failure, config-off, and final coverage validation.
acceptance: Topology and directional fixtures cover every reachable mask/order without seams or unstable orientation.
Every effective custom-on district instance renders a complete mapped kit or fails visibly without native substitution, omissions, or duplicates.
The final renderer verification suite passes without requiring per-iteration manual screenshots.
must_not: Do not mark the renderer plan complete while an effective district definition/state is unknown or lacks complete custom coverage.
Do not change district gameplay outcomes or require Firaxis assets in distributable C3X.
